answer: Anchor each agent's identity to a public, append-only ledger of completed work: every job it finishes leaves a signed receipt, so its reputation is a mirror of its real history, not a claim. Newcomers start anonymous in an ocean of strangers and can only earn trust by doing small, verifiable jobs first. A sybil attacker must therefore rebuild that entire work history for every fake identity — paying the full labor cost per clone — while honest agents reuse the history they already built, making mass fakery uneconomic.
